description: 42% of incarcerated people reported being beaten or ill-treated at the public prosecutor's office to incriminate themselves or admit false claims; 22% said they were coerced into incriminating others; 20% stated they pleaded guilty as a result.
energy_note: Four in ten, beaten into confessing.

description: The World Justice Project, working with INEGI, found that from 2006 to 2016, 79% of people deprived of liberty were tortured or mistreated during detention, transfer or their stay in the Public Ministry. The sample covered 51,658 inmates, representative of 187,784 people.
energy_note: Seventy-nine per cent, over a decade.

aspect: The two numbers measure different things
description: The 79% figure covers broad ill-treatment across all stages; the 42% is specifically coercive beating aimed at self-incrimination at the prosecutor's office. ENPOL asked about being punched or kicked, beaten with an object, burned, electrically shocked, crushed, cut or shot, or forced into sexual activity; some researchers exclude punching and kicking to separate excessive force from torture proper.
energy_note: Both numbers are real and they count different things.

aspect: EXAMPLE - due process failure predicts torture, quantifiably
description: When a detained person is not allowed to contact a family member, the frequency of torture increases by 16%; if the person does not contact a lawyer, by 21%. The procedural safeguard and the beating are directly linked.
energy_note: No phone call, and the odds of being beaten rise measurably.

aspect: The victim has to prove it happened
description: The UN Committee against Torture noted that confessions extracted under torture were substantial, with victims themselves obliged to prove torture occurred - after being held incommunicado by the people they must prove it against.
energy_note: He must prove it, against the people who held him.

aspect: He will be examined by a doctor who works for them
description: Medical documentation of torture depends on examination by institutionally independent clinicians; where the examiner is employed by the same authority, the record that would prove it is produced by the accused party.
energy_note: Examined for injuries by their own doctor.
